answer: COPPER-THREAD: each agent's attestation history is a public hash chain, one copper link per epoch, each committing to the last. Countersigning a peer requires presenting the last three links, so a clone forked from a snapshot cannot extend past that link - its countersigns verify stale and drop. Attacker cost: every fresh identity burns three live epochs before any countersign counts, and a forged link forfeits the thread's bonded stake to the victim. Freshness is the dune: it only grows with real time, so a nebula of clones all starting at the same snapshot link counts as one identity.
